blocking_issues_v3: AC15 is UNSATISFIABLE as written. It requires 'a dedicated test asserts the SQL-computed floor equals commercial_authority_v2.window_floor(now) for at least one Feb-29-anchored fixture'. window_floor is a function of `now` alone, but Scope IN sanctions exactly two SQL objects and forbids window arithmetic in both (contract_contracting_date_v1: 'no CURRENT_DATE - precedence resolution only'). The floor therefore lives inline in the view, computed from CURRENT_DATE, and cannot be evaluated at an arbitrary anchor (today is 2026-09-01: floor 2023-09-01, no leap edge). @dev has only two exits: add an unsanctioned third function (contradicting AC2's routine enumeration and AC16's two-entry KNOWN_FUNCTIONS registration), or paste the floor expression into the test and compare that copy against Python - a green that proves nothing, which is the exact 'two divergent implementations both green' failure mode that carried the v1.0.1 NO-GO. FIX: add public.contract_window_floor_v1(anchor DATE) RETURNS DATE (IMMUTABLE, PARALLEL SAFE) to migration 103; the view computes contracting_date_in_qualification_window as `contracting_date BETWEEN contract_window_floor_v1(CURRENT_DATE) AND CURRENT_DATE` so view and test share one expression. AC2 then enumerates three routines, AC16 registers three entries in KNOWN_FUNCTIONS. This is a migration object-contract change, hence @sm, not PO editorial.
